Abstract
A growing body of current research highlights intrusion detection as a pivotal area 
of study within Internet of Things (IoT) networks, demonstrating its potential to 
enhance operational efficiency. The high diversity of IoT devices, their protocols and 
standards, and their limited computational resources have led to the appearance 
of novel security challenges. However, traditional security solutions to intrusion 
detection systems (IDS) are often unable to counter evolving new attack patterns on 
an overwhelming volume of records with insufficient feature diversity. The advent of 
increased computational power, coupled with accelerated network data traffic and 
reduced computing costs, has enabled researchers across disciplines to use deep 
learning (DL) techniques in IDS datasets to provide high accuracy and real-time 
detection. In this context, first, this study applies Kernel Principal Component Analysis 
(KPCA) to reduce the dimensionality of the dataset while preserving meaningful 
class distinctions. Subsequently, the Lévy flight mechanism is employed to identify 
functional feature sets to increase diversity in the search process. In addition, this 
work integrates deep learning models and addresses prevailing gaps in existing 
intrusion detection research, focusing on their classification performance and 
robustness against vulnerabilities. Additionally, we optimize Deep Neural Networks 
with Long Short-Term Memory architecture (DNN-LSTM) using the adaptive Lévy 
flight Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA) to fine-tune hyperparameters, 
improving anomaly detection efficacy. The proposed approach is evaluated using 
the CIC-IDS 2017, TON-IoT, and NSL-KDD datasets, with experimental results that 
indicate that the DNN-LSTM model significantly improves detection accuracy, 
particularly for novel or small-sample attack scenarios, outperforming standalone DL 
models. Empirical analysis further reveals that our approach surpasses state-of-the-
art deep neural networks across several key performance metrics, underscoring its 
effectiveness in advancing intrusion detection research.

Remarkably, by using the IDS datasets testing, this work rigorously attempts to assess 
the generalization capacities of DL models overcome significantly the class imbalance

approach systematically addresses this gap. Data is growing exponentially; thus, know­

To leverage the practical utility of high-dimensional Intrusion Detection System (IDS)

an effective intrusion detection system. Concurrently, the adaptive Lévy flight Grasshop­

with LSTM, the proposed IDS model overcomes the limitations of traditional intru­
sion detection techniques, achieving higher detection accuracy and providing a robust, 
adaptable solution to modern IoT network security challenges. Furthermore, our model 
demonstrates superior performance compared to several standalone deep learning mod­
els across three benchmark datasets. Experimental evaluations using the CICIDS2017, 
NSL-KDD, and TON-IoT datasets assess the framework’s performance in multiclass 
classification scenarios, underscoring its efficacy in IoT intrusion detection tasks.
On the other hand, intrusion detection systems have been essential in detecting net­
work intrusions and anomalies. A number of scholars have encouraged the adoption 
of deep learning techniques in IDSs to mitigate the threat posed by network intruders. 
Nonetheless, the majority of previously suggested IDSs have been unable to demon­
strate a significant reduction in false alarms, bias, and intelligent exploration methods. 
To address the aforementioned issues, investigating hybrid deep learning technologies 
provides a feasible approach, utilising their proven effectiveness in this field. Thanks to 
advances in deep learning over the last decade, we investigated the conjunction of Deep 
Neural Networks with Long Short-Term Memory architecture (DNN-LSTM) model 
for detecting anomalies in network traffic. Subsequently, the Lévy flight mechanism is 
employed to identify functional feature sets to increase diversity in the search process. 
The suggested model employs the Levy flight with the GOA optimisation technique to 
refine the hyperparameters of the DNN-LSTM. The effectiveness of the proposed model 
is tested and assessed using the most frequently used datasets as CIC-IDS 2017, TON-

3  Preliminaries
Researchers have so far concentrated on creating IDSs for particular IoT technologies 
and scenarios, sometimes using a distributed design that necessitates the installation 
of agents on IoT devices. However, these methods lack flexibility because they must be 
manually adjusted when the monitored IoT network changes. They are too intrusive 
for devices already limited in their ability to run an IDS instance in addition to their 
intended task, giving attackers even more opportunity to carry out modern attacks on 
those devices. To address this issue, we design a new IDS model based on a metaheuris­
tic system that uses hybrid deep-learning methods to improve the detection of known 
and unknown intrusions. Our system incorporates privacy-preserving strategies for 
managing sensitive IoT data while seamlessly integrating anomaly-based detection tech­
niques. Unlike typical machine learning methods, nowadays, deep learning technology 
offers a novel approach to analyzing multi-feature intrusion data since it can automati­
cally learn data features without human interaction. Intrusion detection can effectively 
use the feature information between each data set and solve the problem of rapid gradi­
ent diffusion and weak generalization ability; therefore, in the following subsections, we 
discuss feature seelction and evolutionary methods.

6   Conclusion and future direction
In the current century, contemporary deep learning-based intrusion detection mecha­
nisms face significant challenges in IoT environments, primarily due to their reliance 
on static selection strategy that cannot adapt to evolving attack patterns. Also, it can 
suffer from high false-positive rates exacerbated by class imbalances in IoT protocols, 
along with computational inefficiencies that hinder deployment on resource-constrained 
IoT devices. Existing limitations underscore the need for more adaptive and efficient 
solutions tailored to IoT security requirements. Since the decisions of anomaly-based 
intrusion detection systems (IDS) are highly dependent on the characteristics of typi­
cal traffic used for parameter optimization, accurate choices become more complex 
when the expected behavior of network traffic changes over time due to internal and 
external influences. To address the aforementioned drawbacks, our work first tackles 
the issue of quality feature structure and critical gaps through Kernel Principal Compo­
nent Analysis (KPCA) approach combined with an optimized DNN-LSTM deep learn­
ing architecture. The proposed method automatically selects the hyperparameter of the

Abstract: A growing body of current research highlights intrusion detection as a pivotal area of study within Internet of Things (IoT) networks, demonstrating its potential to enhance operational efficiency. The high diversity of IoT devices, their protocols and standards, and their limited computational resources have led to the appearance of novel security challenges. However, traditional security solutions to intrusion detection systems (IDS) are often unable to counter evolving new attack patterns on an overwhelming volume of records with insufficient feature diversity. The advent of increased computational power, coupled with accelerated network data traffic and reduced computing costs, has enabled researchers across disciplines to use deep learning (DL) techniques in IDS datasets to provide high accuracy and real-time detection. In this context, first, this study applies Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) to reduce the dimensionality of the dataset while preserving meaningful class distinctions. Subsequently, the Lévy flight mechanism is employed to identify functional feature sets to increase diversity in the search process. In addition, this work integrates deep learning models and addresses prevailing gaps in existing intrusion detection research, focusing on their classification performance and robustness against vulnerabilities. Additionally, we optimize Deep Neural Networks with Long Short-Term Memory architecture (DNN-LSTM) using the adaptive Lévy flight Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA) to fine-tune hyperparameters, improving anomaly detection efficacy. The proposed approach is evaluated using the CIC-IDS 2017, TON-IoT, and NSL-KDD datasets, with experimental results that indicate that the DNN-LSTM model significantly improves detection accuracy, particularly for novel or small-sample attack scenarios, outperforming standalone DL models. Empirical analysis further reveals that our approach surpasses state-of-the- art deep neural networks across several key performance metrics, underscoring its effectiveness in advancing intrusion detection research.
